REQ-DATETIME-025/REQ-DATETIME-025-a deliberate decisions-taken-where-the-specification-is-silent a quantity finer than the value is converted to its precision and truncated, so @2014-01-01 + 1 hour is @2014-01-01, as fhirpath.js and the Java engine both answer (rule 1); the case follows 3.0.0's table, which gives hours to DateTime and Time only, and its "unsupported unit for the type" error
REQ-DATETIME-025/REQ-DATETIME-025-b deliberate decisions-taken-where-the-specification-is-silent a quantity finer than the value is converted to its precision and truncated, so + 30 minutes leaves the Date as it is, as fhirpath.js and the Java engine both answer (rule 1); the case follows 3.0.0's "unsupported unit for the type" error
REQ-DATETIME-025/REQ-DATETIME-025-c deliberate decisions-taken-where-the-specification-is-silent a quantity finer than the value is converted to its precision and truncated toward zero, so - 1 second leaves the Date as it is, as fhirpath.js answers (the Java engine shifts at full precision, 2013-12-31, which 3.0.0's @2014 - 1 month example contradicts); the case follows 3.0.0's "unsupported unit for the type" error
REQ-DATETIME-025/REQ-DATETIME-025-d deliberate decisions-taken-where-the-specification-is-silent a quantity finer than the value is converted to its precision and truncated, so + 1 millisecond leaves the Date as it is, as fhirpath.js and the Java engine both answer (rule 1); the case follows 3.0.0's "unsupported unit for the type" error
REQ-DATETIME-025/REQ-DATETIME-025-e deliberate decisions-taken-where-the-specification-is-silent a quantity finer than the value is converted to its precision and truncated, so + 1 's' leaves the Date as it is, as fhirpath.js and the Java engine both answer (rule 1); the case follows 3.0.0's "unsupported unit for the type" error
REQ-DATETIME-025/REQ-DATETIME-025-f deliberate decisions-taken-where-the-specification-is-silent a quantity finer than the value is converted to its precision and truncated, so + 1 'h' leaves the Date as it is, as fhirpath.js and the Java engine both answer (rule 1); the case follows 3.0.0's table and 2.0.0's definite-duration error
REQ-DATETIME-037/REQ-DATETIME-037-b deliberate remaining-gaps the boundary of a DateTime with no offset takes the offset that makes the instant earliest, +14:00, as the official suite and the Java engine have it; the case follows 3.0.0's example, which writes none, as fhirpath.js answers
REQ-DATETIME-038/REQ-DATETIME-038-b deliberate remaining-gaps the boundary of a DateTime with no offset takes the offset that makes the instant latest, -12:00, as the official suite and the Java engine have it; the case follows 3.0.0's example, which writes none, as fhirpath.js answers (the time, 08:59:59.999, is the example's and fhirpath.js's, where the Java engine gives 08:00:59.999)
